I found the root cause: `evaluate_xfail_marks()` is cached in `item._store[xfailed_key]` during setup (and again at call start, still before the test body runs). When the marker is added *inside* the test, the cached value is `None` and `pytest_runtest_makereport` never re-evaluates, so the call report stays a failure.

The fix is to re-evaluate the xfail marks in `pytest_runtest_makereport` when no evaluation result is available. Let me apply it and immediately verify with the reproduction plus the existing xfail tests.

I found the root cause: `evaluate_xfail_marks()` is cached in `item._store[xfailed_key]` during setup (and again at call start, still before the test body runs). When the marker is added *inside* the test, the cached value is `None` and `pytest_runtest_makereport` never re-evaluates, so the call report stays a failure.

The fix is to re-evaluate the xfail marks in `pytest_runtest_makereport` when no evaluation result is available. Let me apply it and immediately verify with the reproduction plus the existing xfail tests.

import io

When the marker is added *inside* the test, the cached value is `None` and `pytest_runtest_makereport` never re-evaluates, so the call report stays a failure.

The fix is to re-evaluate the xfail marks in `pytest_runtest_makereport` when no evaluation result is available. Let me apply it and immediately verify with the reproduction plus the existing xfail tests.

I found the root cause: `evaluate_xfail_marks()` is cached in `item._store[xfailed_key]` during setup (and again at call start, still before the test body runs). When the marker is added *inside* the test, the cached value is `None` and `pytest_runtest_makereport` never re-evaluates, so the call report stays a failure.

The fix is to re-evaluate the xfail marks in `pytest_runtest_makereport` when no evaluation result is available. Let me apply it and immediately verify with the reproduction plus the existing xfail tests.
